kernel_of_truth: Three real things sit under the dome's eclipse claims. Eclipses do disturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw H at the dome's stations really was 13-19 nT low. The dome's quiet-day precondition is good practice; its Boulder statistic is well defined and exactly reproducible, and this day failed it. And across the dome's stations the eclipse-window Z residuals do increase northward in its FSF order, more than on any of 19 ordinary days. None of that saves the claims: ordinary days produce the same raw H; the PRED-095 card's H anomaly met neither its claim nor its falsifier; the dome's own named component shows the latitude ordering at about half the formula's -10.9-baseline size and far below its x1.672 size; the contact-phase signature it calls ECM-unique is absent where it would have stood out; and a sunset eclipse under standard Sq physics also produces larger effects where the Sun stood higher - in the north. Being right about the ordering does not favour dome physics. A void test is not a confirmation, and the dome's own live scoreboard still reads PENDING.

anticipated_objections.objection: Dome defender: "By its own falsification line PRED-095 was not falsified."
anticipated_objections.response: Correct, and we now say so in the headline and in dome_favourable_findings. The card's claimed -17.8 nT was not observed either; the result sits in the gap the card leaves between its claim and its falsifier, a gap ordinary days also fall into.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: "Your joint fit only disfavours the formula; you said rejected last time."
anticipated_objections.response: Rev3 never used the joint fit; the curmudgeon proposed it and warned the WLS se might be too small. Calibrated on control days it is: the -10.9 baseline is disfavoured, not excluded; the x1.672 specification the dome actually published for 2026 is excluded in every variant.

anticipated_objections.objection: Skeptic: "You are now going soft on the dome - PRED-095 is no longer falsified."
anticipated_objections.response: We score registrations on their own terms and components, the same way we scored our own B1-M-001 by its pre-registered metric (non-diagnostic). The Z paragraph and Tier 1 still fail with model attribution; the card does not, by its own lines. Shielding nothing and overclaiming nothing is the point of the symmetry rule.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: "The northward-increasing Z residual is FSF physics."
anticipated_objections.response: It has the FSF shape at half the formula size, fits barely better than flat, and a solar-elevation weighting (standard Sq physics for a sunset eclipse) fits about as well or better. Shape ordering does not discriminate; amplitude goes against the formula.
